transcript.text: Here's how to invest your first $1,000
if you want to build real wealth. Step
one, get back your money. So, what I
mean by that? You have a certain amount
of income that you make from whatever
job that you have. There's a certain
amount of spend that you spend every
single month. The goal is to get that as
close to zero as humanly possible. That
means you only shop at Goodwill going
forward. That means you only buy
second-hand clothes or none at all. That
means that you only eat brown bag
lunches wherever you go. You never eat
out. And if you're like, "Man, that
sounds intense." It's like, "Yeah, so is
being poor." So, the more dry powder you
have, the more cash that you can deploy.
Step two, get back your time. So, right
now, you probably are spending time you
aren't making money on. So, that means
you're spending time watching Netflix.
That means you're looking at things you
shouldn't be looking at. You're going
out on nights and spending money that
you don't have to impress people whose
lives you don't want. So, once you have
your time and your money, then you
research. So, that means you look at
your current skill set and you say,
"Okay, which of these skill sets can I
double down on and take to the next
level?" And once you identify this is
the one that has the highest earning
potential, you move to step four. You
apply the time that you just got back
and the money you now have from the
savings towards doubling that down as
fast as possible. Then, you repeat over
and over again until you walk in the
skill and you start earning higher wage.
Now, the key here is people talk about
10,000 hours of mastery. It's more
about, and this is Naval Ravikant,
10,000 iterations. So, the goal is to
get as many cycles in as humanly
possible, not wait as long as possible.
And then, finally, step six, once you do
start winning, don't backslide with your
time and don't let your lifestyle creep
up. Once you're making more, keep your
lifestyle low, take the spread, and then
double down again.
